title: T1090 — Proxy
subtitle: Watch one attack pass through a port-redirector proxy in eight steps.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Implant beacon start
steps.caption: An implant on Victim A starts its beacon. It connects outward to one address: a rented port-redirector proxy. The implant's configuration does not contain the real C2 address.
steps.defender: the firewall records a new egress flow from one workstation.

fields.detail: An implant on Victim A starts its beacon. It connects outward to one address: a rented port-redirect

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Packet to proxy
steps.caption: The company firewall forwards the packet to the proxy on the internet. The log line shows the source host and the proxy's IP address and port. No attacker-owned address appears anywhere yet.
steps.defender: the destination is a hosting-provider IP you have never seen before.

fields.detail: The company firewall forwards the packet to the proxy on the internet. The log line shows the source

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Proxy forwards to C2
steps.caption: The port redirector accepts the connection and opens a second one to the real C2 server. This leg happens on the internet, outside your logging. Your team cannot see it at all.
steps.defender: your visibility ends at the proxy IP - that is the design goal of the attacker.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: C2 reply through proxy
steps.caption: The C2 server answers. The reply travels back along the same path: C2 → proxy → firewall → Victim A. The implant receives its first command.
steps.defender: the reply content stays invisible without TLS inspection; the flow shape is what you can still measure.

fields.detail: The C2 server answers. The reply travels back along the same path: C2 → proxy → firewall → Victim A.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Defender view: the proxy hides the C2
steps.caption: The SOC reviews the flow. The destination is unknown but ordinary-looking, and no blocklist matches. The channel looks clean even though it carries attacker commands.
steps.defender: judge the behavior - steady timing, first-seen ASN - not the IP alone.

fields.detail: The SOC reviews the flow. The destination is unknown but ordinary-looking, and no blocklist matches.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Second victim added
steps.caption: The attacker spreads to Victim B, perhaps with a phishing reply or a stolen credential. The new implant uses the same proxy hop. Now two hosts beacon to one destination.
steps.defender: a second host to the same first-seen IP is a strong scope signal.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Log trail on the firewall
steps.caption: The firewall log now shows a clean trail: two sources, one destination, steady intervals. The proxy IP is the one constant across both victims. The C2 behind it stays hidden.
steps.defender: the proxy IP is your pivot - everything else in the case hangs from it.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC pivot
steps.caption: The analyst pivots on the proxy IP across 30 days of logs, finds both victims, blocks the address, and reports the case. The attacker may rotate the proxy, but the behavioral rules keep firing.
steps.defender: hunt the pattern, not the address - rotation does not defeat timing and ASN rules.
